
Assembly of the BBD nanopore reads with Flye. Commands for this step were run in `flye/`.

## **Step 2: Assembly**

Moved into the `flye` folder and made a symbolic link to the BBD read data, so the large file sn't copied.

```{bash}
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/flye # Change directonary
ln -s /pvol/data/metagenome_assembly/bbd_0.1.fastq.gz . #symbolick link 
```

Made a new shell script called [run_flye_bbd.sh](flye/run_flye_bbd.sh) and saved it in the `flye` folder.

Submitted the job and followed it's progress in the queue.

```{bash}
sbatch run_flye_bbd.sh
```

Following in the queue

```{bash}
squeue
```

The job ran for about 45 min.

Checked that flye worked with `sacct` (job 470) instead of the slurm log prints "Finished" even if flye fails.

```{bash}
sacct -j 470 --format=JobID,State,MaxRSS,Elapsed # The state coloumn says completed, so all good!
```

The state column said COMPLETED, so the run worked.

Final assembly was then assessed

```{bash}
ls -l bbd/assembly.fasta
```
